title: SDK adapter onboarding and failure-mode lab playbook (2025)
author: Priya Nair
body:
Summary:
This playbook covers onboarding for new SDK adapter integrations, the lab exercises engineers run to prove reliability and cost behavior, a failure-mode matrix for common adapter faults, and canonical fixes for the incidents we see most in production. Audience: SDK engineers, integration partners, and support engineers doing triage and permanent fixes.

Scope and intent:
- Scope: language/platform adapters mapping a customer call surface (HTTP/GRPC/SDK) onto Redwood’s runtime API (proxy, dual-write, or direct).
- Intent: lower mean-time-to-detect and mean-time-to-fix for adapter incidents by standardizing tests, telemetry, and remediation.
- Exclusions: runtime kernel-level issues and third-party cloud outages (see related runbooks).

When to use this playbook:
1) Onboarding a new adapter (partner or internal)
2) Triage when adapter errors spike after a release
3) Oncall handling of persistent customer-facing degradations
4) Postmortem follow-ups for adapter incidents

Key components covered:
- Local lab harness (dx-adapter-lab)
- Telemetry contract and sampling
- Failure-mode matrix and canonical fixes
- Oncall escalation and permanent remediation checklist
- Example CLI commands, sample JSON requests, and test payloads

Readiness checklist (pre-onboarding):
- [ ] Dedicated GitHub repo with a CODEOWNERS entry
- [ ] Integration manifest (adapter.yaml) with implementation and config fields
- [ ] Unit and integration tests in CI; coverage >= 50% for request/response logic
- [ ] Contract tests against local dx-adapter-lab passing in CI
- [ ] Telemetry emission validated (see Telemetry section)
- [ ] Security review booked if the adapter touches customer data

Adapter manifest (adapter.yaml) example:
---
name: my-llm-adapter
version: 0.1.0
owner: team-llm-adapters
exposed_protocols: [http, grpc]
timeout_ms: 3000
retry_policy: { max_retries: 2, backoff_ms: 200 }
---
(Commit this at the repo root and include an example config in the README.)

Telemetry contract:
- Required events:
  - adapter.request.start (tags: adapter, operation, request_id, tenant_id)
  - adapter.request.end (tags: adapter, operation, request_id, tenant_id, status_code, duration_ms)
  - adapter.cache.hit/miss (tags: adapter, key_hash, upstream_model)
- Sampling: 100% for errors and >=95th latency; 1% baseline for successful sub-100ms requests
- Traces: span names adapter.{operation}.start / adapter.{operation}.end; link runtime.trace_id where available

Failure-mode matrix (from support incidents):
| Symptom | Likely root cause | Detect signal | Immediate mitigation | Permanent fix owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5xx errors from adapter | runtime contract mismatch or invalid auth | per-route 5xx rate; adapter.request.end.status_code=500 | 1) Shift traffic to canary variant 2) Turn off feature flag | adapter-owner + runtime-infra |
| Elevated p50/p95 latency | blocking sync call or unbounded retries | latency heatmap; adapter.request.end.duration_ms spikes | Add circuit breaker / short-circuit heavy path | adapter-owner |
| Tokenization divergences | wrong prompt encoding or charset mismatch | user complaints + golden prompt eval failures | Pin to reference encoder; flag affected versions | ml-infra + adapter-owner |
| Cache poisoning / stale KV | cache key collision across tenants | hit/miss ratio anomalies; duplicate cache.key_hash | Per-tenant cache isolation; invalidate keys | adapter-owner + platform |

Canonical fixes:
1) 5xx from schema drift:
   - Check payload shape with local contract tests: dx-adapter-lab contract run --manifest adapter.yaml
   - For intentional schema changes, publish a versioned manifest and add a runtime compatibility shim (runtime-infra deploys the shim).
2) Latency from a blocking dependency:
   - Temporarily move long ops to an async worker returning 202 with x-retry-after; for sustained load add resilient buffering (kafka/queue).
3) Intermittent auth failures:
   - Rotate short-lived credentials, add a token refresh path, and back off on 401 to avoid a thundering herd.
4) Output regressions after an adapter update:
   - Run the golden prompt suite: ./scripts/regression-check.sh --golden ./goldens/default.json; revert and bisect to locate the change.

Oncall triage (first 20 minutes):
1) Scope it: check the per-route dashboard; ping the oncall channel if >5 customers are affected.
2) Quick checks with dx-adapter-detect:
   - dx-adapter-detect --route my-adapter --window 10m --metrics [5xx, p95, throughput]
   - If 5xx > 1% of requests: switch to the fallback adapter via runtime routing policy.
3) Pull traces by request_id from error logs and attach three examples to the PagerDuty ticket.
4) Roll back fast, or split traffic 50/50 with the previous adapter version.
5) For code fixes, cut a hotfix branch and follow the CI hotpatch checklist (forced integration tests plus manual approval).

Permanent remediation checklist:
- Short postmortem linked to the incident ticket (owner: adapter-owner).
- Add the failing payloads to canonical regression tests.
- Bump the adapter.yaml version and record the compatibility rationale.
- Add a telemetry golden (synthetic trace) to the nightly contract run.
- Add a canary gate to the deploy pipeline where it makes sense.

Lab exercises (required before staging acceptance):
1) Failure injection: inject 10% upstream 500s and confirm backpressure cuts retries and logs useful error codes. Command: dx-adapter-lab inject --mode upstream-500 --rate 10
2) Latency profiling: 10k requests with p95 under 250ms. Command: dx-adapter-lab load --concurrency 50 --requests 10000 --assert p95<250
3) Cost profiling: tokenized load to measure average tokens per request and estimated cost with cost-sim.
4) Regression validation: golden prompt suite with no semantic drift beyond allowed thresholds.

Example diagnostics:
- Sample request JSON (generation):
{
  "operation": "generation",
  "model": "gpt-redwood-0.1",
  "prompt": "Summarize the following text...",
  "max_tokens": 128
}

- CLI commands:
  - Contract test: dx-adapter-lab contract run --manifest adapter.yaml
  - Local sandbox: dx-adapter-lab sandbox --port 8081 --env local
  - Trace fetch: runtime-cli traces fetch --filter "service:adapter and request_id:1234" --output sample-trace.json

Dashboards:
- Adapter per-route SLO: /dashboards/adapter-per-route
- Telemetry golden traces: /dashboards/adapter-golden-traces
- Latency heatmap and errors: /dashboards/adapter-latency-errors

Operational knobs and defaults:
- timeout_ms: 3000 (default)
- max_retries: 2 (for idempotent ops)
- circuit_breaker_threshold: 5 failures / 1m window
- cache_ttl_seconds: 60 (per-tenant isolation recommended)

Best practices for SDK authors:
- Keep adapter code idempotent under at-least-once retries.
- Use async paths for non-critical enrichment.
- Emit structured logs with request_id and version tag.
- Test that the adapter honors runtime feature flags.

Escalation and ownership:
- Runtime faults (5xx / contract drift): adapter-owner -> runtime-infra -> eng-sre
- Security-sensitive regressions: adapter-owner -> security -> legal
- Billing/cost regressions: adapter-owner -> finance -> product

Acceptance criteria for production rollout:
1) All lab exercises green, artifacts uploaded to the artifact store.
2) Telemetry contract tests green in nightly CI for two weeks with synthetic traffic.
3) SLO smoke tests show p50<120ms, p95<250ms on baseline traffic.
4) Post-release monitoring runbook documented in the repo README.

FAQ:
Q: My adapter needs specialized model tokens or encoding?
A: Document it in adapter.yaml, add an adapter-specific token-metering test, and ask runtime-infra for a feature flag.

Q: Large-batch requests take longer than 3s?
A: Use the async buffer pattern (202 plus a status endpoint) and raise manifest.timeout_ms to match.
